CONFIDENCE: 0.37
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows features of an ortho-disubstituted benzenoid acid.  

Key matches for o-hydroxybenzoic (salicylic) acid, O=C(O)c1cccc(O)c1 (candidate 8):  
• Very strong C=O (acid/aryl-conjugated) stretch at 1680 cm⁻¹.  
• Strong aromatic C=C stretch at 1600 cm⁻¹ and C–H stretches at 3073 cm⁻¹, typical for an aromatic lacking aliphatic C–H.  
• Intense ring-breathing doublet 1009/990 cm⁻¹ plus 1033 cm⁻¹, characteristic of 1,2-disubstituted benzenes.  
• Strong 1180 and 1265 cm⁻¹ bands correspond to C–O stretches of phenolic and carboxylic groups; 1411 and 1454 cm⁻¹ fit O–H in-plane bending of the intramolecularly H-bonded salicylate ring.  
• Peaks near 864 and 835 cm⁻¹ match out-of-plane O–H and C–H bends seen in salicylic acid; 771 and 700 cm⁻¹ accord with ortho-disubstituted ring deformations.  
• No bands for aliphatic C–H (~2900 cm⁻¹) or amide/azo S=O/NO₂ stretches, disfavoring other candidates.  
Overall, the presence of a conjugated carboxylic acid carbonyl, a phenolic O–H, and an ortho-disubstituted benzene pattern best fit candidate 8.
